full.answer: The maximum input voltage on the VIN pad / DC jack of the Arduino UNO R4 WiFi is 24 V.

The minimum VIN / DC jack input voltage for the Arduino Mega 2560 Rev3 is 7 V.

The Nicla Vision's maximum battery input voltage (VBATT) is 4.7 V.
The Nano RP2040 Connect's maximum USB input voltage is 5.25 V.

The Recommended Operating Conditions table lists the VIN input voltage maximum as 32 V (min 6 V, typ 7.0 V) [ABX00063 p.7], while the Features section states the VIN input voltage range as 6-24V [ABX00063 p.3].

full.answer: The UNO R4 WiFi has a recommended VIN range of 6-24 V, giving a maximum of 24 V, while the GIGA R1 WiFi has a maximum VIN of 32 V. Therefore, the GIGA R1 WiFi accepts the higher maximum VIN.

The Portenta C33's typical deep sleep current is 86 µA (ABX00074 p.9), while the Nicla Vision's is 374 uA (ABX00051 p.8); therefore, the Portenta C33 uses less current in deep sleep.
The UNO R3 has 2 kB SRAM from its ATMega328P processor, while the Nano Every has 6 kB SRAM from its ATMega4809 processor; therefore, the Nano Every has more SRAM.

full.answer: The main microcontroller on the Arduino UNO R3 is the ATmega328P.
The MKR WiFi 1010 uses the Nina W102 wireless module, which is based on the ESP32.
The MKR WAN 1310 uses the Murata CMWX1ZZABZ LoRa module.
The Nicla Sense ME is powered by the nRF52832 SoC within the ANNA-B112 module.
The Nicla Vision uses the LSM6DSOX 6-axis IMU.
The Nano 33 BLE Rev2's NINA B306 module has 1 MB of Flash and 256 kB of RAM.

Header pin 2, labeled A0/DAC0, can be used as a DAC output.
On the Arduino Nano Every, pin 1 is D13, which is the SPI SCK (SPI clock).
The reset pin is on the J2 Fins connector at pin P5, listed as RESET (Digital).
